newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stock index futures end lower on whipsaw day.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stock index futures end lower on whipsaw day.

text.p: A day of whipsaw price swings left U.S. stock index futures lower at the end of pit trading on Tuesday, with traders still bullish and the key December S&P 500 stock index futures contract closing on a rally.
Despite the approaching holiday, liquidity on the market was strong, one trader said.
"We had one of our better days in the last maybe two or three weeks in terms of people coming in the market," he said.
That did not stop December S&P 500s from taking a wild ride, however, from a early morning all-time high of 765.30 to an intraday low less than an hour later of 754.00.

The contract opened higher than Monday's settlement, saw a quick and orderly sell-off by major dealers, then took off on a half-hour rally that peaked at the all-time high. The run was fueled principally by a higher bond market, which took its cue from new data on consumer confidence, traders said.
The Conference Board reported early Tuesday that U.S. consumer confidence held steady in November at 107.3 from a revised October level of 107.3 and below estimates of 109.00.
Bond futures moved up on the data, carrying December S&Ps with them. Then December S&Ps continued rising on momentum trading even after bond futures lost steam, traders said.

Even as the contract soared, partly on short-covering, technical analysts warned the market looked overbought and could correct. At technical resistance around the contract high, December S&Ps reversed course and fell. Big sell programs came into play down to the day's low, traders said.
"It looked real good, then it turned around in a dive. There were some programs all the way," one pit trader said. "It was a pretty precipitous fall."
Bottoming at 754.00, December S&Ps tried a comeback but failed to muster much strength before the closing bell. "We tried to bounce back up but couldn't do it," a trader said.
The day's low was above Monday's low of 750.20, a pattern technical analysts said would have to hold for the market to maintain a bullish tone.
Before Tuesday, the previous December S&P 500 contract high was 762.25, set Monday night in GLOBEX trading.

At the end of pit trading, December S&P 500s were off 2.60 points to 757.35, KBT Value Lines were off 3.60 points to 681.40, Nikkeis were off 5.0 to 21,415.0, Midcap 400s were off 0.85 to 256.15 and Nasdaq 100s were off 0.10 to 825.65.
